newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks get reprieve on rate front, oils jump.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks get reprieve on rate front, oils jump.

text.p: U.S. blue chips finished solidly higher after a tumultuous session that saw stocks and bonds overcome steep early losses.

The Dow industrials rose 32 points to close unofficially at 5648, after falling more than 50 points in the first minutes of the session on mounting worries about interest rates and news of the U.S. military action against Iraq.
However, analysts warned the strong finish masked continued uncertainty about rates, noting most of the Dow's came from oil stocks, which surged on higher crude prices.
The rebound in stocks began with release of the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index of manufacturing activity for the month of August.

The index, which rose to 52.6 from 50.2 in July, showed continued strength in the manufacturing sector but fell short of forecasts for a 52.9 reading, leaving sentiment unsettled on the timing and magnitude of the Federal Reserve's next move.

"After NAPM, which was generally in line with forecasts, you can still make a case both ways," said First Albany chief investment officer Hugh Johnson. "It left markets with reason to believe the Fed will move and reason to believe it won't."

Late in the session, stocks got another boost from a soft Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc retail sales report, which showed seasonally adjusted retail sales in the U.S. rose just 0.8 percent in the four weeks of August compared to fiscal July.
The tame growth surprised analysts, who had expected more of a jump due to back-to-school sales, and sent the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond to a solid 21/32 gain, pulling the yield down to 7.06 percent.
Oil stocks were the session's standouts, with Texaco Inc up 3-1/8 to 91-7/8, Exxon Corp up 2-1/4 to 83-3/4 and Mobil Corp up 2-3/8 to 115-3/8.

The jump in oil stocks tracked crude oil prices, which surged following the U.S. attack on Iraq. NYMEX October crude futures contracts closed up $1.15 to $23.40 a barrel after hitting a contract high of $25.25 during the day.
The spike in oil prices boded ill for energy-hungry sectors, however, and sent the Dow Jones Transportation index tumbling 19 points to 2026.
"Oil stocks turned the market positive, but with higher oil prices come tougher times for the Transports," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Particularly hard hit were airlines, with Delta Air Lines Inc down two to 68-7/8, United Airlines parent company UAL Corp off 1/2 to 47-1/2, and USAir Group Inc down 1/2 to 17-3/8.

In yet another sign of increasing unease on Wall Street, Dean Witter Reynolds said it was reducing its asset allocation model's exposure to stocks and bonds during what the firm's chief investment strategist Peter Canelo said promises to be an extended period of uncertainty.

Canelo said interest rate concerns were the primary reason for raising cash in the model. Stocks now represent 55 percent of the Dean Witter model, down from 60 percent, and bonds account for 20 percent, down from 25 percent.
Cash was increased to 25 percent from 15 percent.
"The problem is this period of uncertainty could last more than a week," Canelo said.
Among individual issues, Intel Corp rose 1-13/16 to 81-5/8 after Robertson Stephens raised its earnings estimates on the company for 1996 and 1997.
Cisco Systems Inc gained one to 53-3/4 after announcing it would acquire privately held Granite Systems Inc for $220 million in stock.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.79 to 1142.29.
The S&P 500 index rose 2.73 to 654.72.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk, 212 859 1721
